rules.when: You report a user-visible change as fixed or done.

use.text: Name the released version that runs and where it is observable, or say plainly that the change is merged but not released.

rules.why: A merge is not a release, and an unmarked merge report misleads.

rules.when: You decide a pull request is ready to merge.

use.text: Take the proof at the exact head you merge, after the last commit, and merge only through the guarded merge path.

rules.why: Any later commit moves the head and voids the proof.

rules.when: You write or change a test.

use.text: Add an integration or end-to-end test that drives the real product, and extend the journey test the change touches. Do not add unit, snapshot or mock-heavy tests.

rules.why: Only a test that drives the real product proves the user's path.

rules.when: The pull request is open and its checks run.

use.text: Do not push again while the checks run. Put every follow-up fix into one push, and run the CI lint locally before the first push.

rules.why: Each push restarts every check, so a lint fix after opening costs a full run.

rules.when: You name or rename a skill that a tool or project ships.

use.text: Prefix it with its source: done-done-, lfm-, sign-off-, first-draft-, byokit-, muxr-, crewhouse-, takeone-.

rules.why: The prefix is how a user knows which tool owns the skill.

default.why: No rule matched. Follow the project's own convention, then add a rule here when it should hold across projects.
